name: KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine)
description: Linux kernel module exposing /dev/kvm; provides the hardware-virtualization primitives (VMX on Intel, SVM on AMD, EL2 on ARM) that Firecracker uses as its VMM substrate. Firecracker is a userspace VMM that talks to KVM via ioctls — KVM handles the heavy CPU/MMU virt; Firecracker handles devices, scheduling, and the API.

name: KVM System fd
description: Handle obtained from open('/dev/kvm'). Used to issue system-level ioctls that affect the whole KVM subsystem (KVM_GET_API_VERSION, KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION, KVM_CREATE_VM, KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE, KVM_GET_MSR_INDEX_LIST). The first thing Firecracker opens at VMM init.

name: KVM VM fd
description: Handle returned by KVM_CREATE_VM on the system fd. Scopes ioctls to one virtual machine — memory layout, irqchip, MSI/IRQ routing, vCPU creation. VM ioctls must be issued from the same process (address space) that created the VM.

name: KVM vCPU fd
description: Handle returned by KVM_CREATE_VCPU on the VM fd. Scopes ioctls to a single virtual CPU — register state (regs/sregs/MSRs/CPUID/FPU/XSAVE), the KVM_RUN entry, LAPIC, MP state. vcpu ioctls should be issued from the thread that will run KVM_RUN; otherwise a thread-local cache may be flushed unnecessarily.

name: KVM Device fd
description: Handle returned by KVM_CREATE_DEVICE. Scopes ioctls to in-kernel emulated devices (e.g. ARM GIC, PMU, vfio). Firecracker uses few in-kernel devices on x86 (most are VirtIO in userspace); on aarch64 the GIC is created via this path.

name: KVM_RUN main loop
description: The vCPU ioctl that enters the guest. Returns when the guest exits — to userspace via shared `kvm_run` mmap struct that carries the exit reason and any per-exit data (MMIO/PIO request, IRQ window, etc.). Firecracker runs one KVM_RUN main loop per vCPU thread; userspace handles the exit, resolves the I/O, and loops back into KVM_RUN.

name: kvm_run shared structure
description: Memory-mapped region (size obtained via KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE) shared between userspace and the kernel for one vCPU. Carries `exit_reason`, per-exit unions (mmio, io, internal, fail_entry, hyperv, system_event), and request flags. Userspace mmaps it once at vCPU init; the kernel writes to it on every KVM_RUN return.

name: KVM_EXIT_MMIO
description: Guest accessed a memory range that wasn't backed by KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION. kvm_run.mmio carries phys_addr, len (1/2/4/8), data[8], is_write. Firecracker uses this to dispatch to its VirtIO device emulators (on aarch64 this is the primary device-MMIO transport; on x86 too for VirtIO-MMIO).

name: KVM_EXIT_IO
description: Guest issued an I/O port instruction (in/out) on x86. kvm_run.io carries direction, size (1/2/4), port, count. Firecracker handles this for legacy serial (port 0x3f8), i8042 keyboard controller (0x60/0x64), and PIT/PIC ports — the minimal legacy device set.

name: KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN
description: Guest issued an architectural reset (triple-fault on x86, PSCI SYSTEM_OFF on ARM). Firecracker treats this as terminal — emits InstanceShutdown via state machine and tears down the microVM.

name: KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY
description: VMX/SVM entry into the guest failed at the hardware-virt level. kvm_run.fail_entry carries hardware_entry_failure_reason and cpu (vCPU number). Common on nested-virt setups (firecracker-microvm/firecracker#668), corrupted vmcs state after botched snapshot restore, or unsupported CPU features.

name: KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR
description: KVM detected an unrecoverable internal inconsistency — emulation impossible, simul exception delivery, unexpected delivery_event. kvm_run.internal carries suberror code and ndata extra registers. Should never happen; if it does, the microVM is unsalvageable.

name: KVM_EXIT_HLT
description: Guest executed HLT in a state where it would block. KVM returns to userspace so it can decide what to do (typically Firecracker's vCPU thread blocks on a futex waiting for an interrupt).

name: KVM_EXIT_IRQ_WINDOW_OPEN
description: Guest interrupt-window is open and userspace had previously requested notification (kvm_run.request_interrupt_window=1). Firecracker uses this to deliver pending IRQs that couldn't be injected synchronously.

name: KVM_EXIT_SYSTEM_EVENT
description: Guest requested a system-level event — SHUTDOWN, RESET, CRASH, S2RAM, SEV_TERM, WAKEUP. kvm_run.system_event.type identifies which. Firecracker handles RESET (warm reset) and SHUTDOWN (terminal).

name: KVM_EXIT_DEBUG
description: Guest hit a debug exception — single-step or hardware breakpoint set via KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG. Used by `firecracker --gdb-socket` flow for in-guest debugging (see fc-docs-gdb-debugging).

name: User Memory Region
description: KVM's mechanism for mapping host userspace memory into guest physical address space. Each region: slot ID (max KVM_USER_MEM_SLOTS), guest_phys_addr, memory_size, userspace_addr, flags (KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES | KVM_MEM_READONLY | KVM_MEM_GUEST_MEMFD). Set via KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION (or _REGION2 for guest_memfd). Firecracker registers one large region for guest RAM at boot; snapshots replay the same regions on restore.

name: Dirty Page Logging
description: Per-region bitmap of pages written by the guest since last query. Enabled by KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES on a memory region; queried via KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG. Backbone of incremental snapshots — Firecracker enables this when taking a diff snapshot to capture only modified pages since the last full.

name: In-kernel IRQchip
description: KVM emulates the IRQ controllers (PIC/IOAPIC on x86, GIC on ARM) inside the kernel rather than in userspace. Created via KVM_CREATE_IRQCHIP (x86) or KVM_CREATE_DEVICE with KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V3 (ARM). Firecracker requires this for low-latency interrupt delivery; switching to userspace irqchip would dramatically increase VM-exit count.

name: GSI Routing Table
description: Maps Global System Interrupts (GSIs) to in-kernel IRQ-line / MSI / hypercall destinations. Set via KVM_SET_GSI_ROUTING; entries are KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_IRQCHIP / _MSI / _HV_SINT. Firecracker programs MSI routes for VirtIO devices to deliver interrupts directly to vCPUs without userspace involvement.

name: irqfd
description: eventfd registered with KVM_IRQFD that, when written, raises a guest IRQ on a configured GSI. Lets userspace devices signal interrupts without the cost of a vCPU ioctl per event. Firecracker uses irqfd extensively for VirtIO ring-event-to-IRQ delivery.

name: ioeventfd
description: eventfd registered with KVM_IOEVENTFD that signals when the guest writes a specific value to a specific I/O port or MMIO address. Lets KVM short-circuit notification of VirtIO doorbell writes — the guest write is consumed in-kernel and the eventfd is signaled, bypassing userspace until the device thread is ready.

name: Guest CPUID control
description: KVM_SET_CPUID2 lets userspace specify the CPUID leaves the guest sees. Firecracker uses CPU templates (T2, T2A, T2CL, T2S, etc.) to mask features for live-migration-safety across host CPU generations. Mismatched CPUID between snapshot-source and -target hosts causes restore to fail.

name: Guest MSR control
description: KVM_GET_MSRS / KVM_SET_MSRS save and restore the guest's Model-Specific Registers. Snapshot/restore uses these to checkpoint per-vCPU state. KVM_GET_MSR_INDEX_LIST enumerates which MSRs the host KVM supports — Firecracker filters out unsupported MSRs to make CPU-template snapshots portable.

name: XSAVE state
description: Extended state (FPU, SSE, AVX, AVX-512, etc.) saved via KVM_GET_XSAVE2 (or KVM_GET_XSAVE for legacy fixed-size). Per-vCPU; included in snapshots. Size depends on enabled XCRs and supported features — KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION(KVM_CAP_XSAVE2) returns the dynamic size.

name: LAPIC state
description: Per-vCPU Local APIC register file (1 KiB), saved via KVM_GET_LAPIC and restored via KVM_SET_LAPIC. Required for snapshot consistency — pending interrupts and timer state live here.

name: vCPU MP State
description: Multiprocessing state of a vCPU: RUNNABLE, UNINITIALIZED, INIT_RECEIVED, HALTED, SIPI_RECEIVED, STOPPED, CHECK_STOP, OPERATING, LOAD. Set/get via KVM_SET_MP_STATE / KVM_GET_MP_STATE. Snapshots restore this so a halted vCPU stays halted on resume.

name: kvm-clock
description: Paravirtualized clock source the guest sees as kvm-clock. Backed by host monotonic clock; survives vCPU migration between host CPUs. Default for Linux guests <5.10; ≥5.10 prefers TSC if stable.

name: TSC control + KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL
description: Lets userspace set the guest's TSC frequency and offset. Required for snapshot restore on a host with a different TSC frequency. KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL must be present; KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ and KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ are the ioctls.

name: VirtIO over MMIO
description: VirtIO transport that uses memory-mapped I/O (vs PCI). Firecracker uses VirtIO-MMIO for all its emulated devices (block, net, vsock, balloon) — keeps the device model minimal vs the PCI alternative. Each device occupies a 4KiB MMIO region; doorbell writes trigger ioeventfds; interrupts via configured GSI/MSI.
